68145-use-of-tobacco-among-north-america.title: North American Indians
68145-use-of-tobacco-among-north-america.creator: Ralph Linton
68145-use-of-tobacco-among-north-america.description: A book by Ralph Linton. At the time of the discovery of America, tobacco was in use over the greater part of the continent. It was not used in the sub-Arctic regions of North America or in the extreme southern part of Southern America. On the west coast of South America and in the Andean highlands it was replaced by another narcotic, coca (_Erythroxylum coca_), from which the modern drug cocaine is extracted.

arxiv-2003-11334.title: ACNMP: Skill Transfer and Task Extrapolation through Learning from Demonstration and Reinforcement Learning via Representation Sharing
arxiv-2003-11334.creator: M. Tuluhan Akbulut, Erhan Oztop, M. Yunus Seker, Honghu Xue, Ahmet E. Tekden, Emre Ugur
arxiv-2003-11334.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by M. Tuluhan Akbulut, Erhan Oztop, M. Yunus Seker, Honghu Xue, Ahmet E. Tekden, Emre Ugur. To equip robots with dexterous skills, an effective approach is to first transfer the desired skill via Learning from Demonstration (LfD), then let the robot improve it by self-exploration via Reinforcement Learning (RL). In this paper, we propose a novel LfD+RL framework, namely Adaptive Conditional Neural Movement Primitives (ACNMP), that allows efficient policy improvement in novel environments and effective skill transfer between different agents.

arxiv-2110-11003.title: The twisted 1-loop invariant and the Jacobian of Ptolemy coordinates
arxiv-2110-11003.creator: Seokbeom Yoon
arxiv-2110-11003.description: Abstract . We present an alternative definition of the twisted 1-loop invariant in terms of the Jacobian of Ptolemy coordinates. As an application, we prove that the twisted 1-loop invariant is equal to the adjoint twisted Alexander polynomial for all hyperbolic once-punctured torus bundles.

arxiv-2111-13592.title: Multi-criticality and related bifurcation in accretion discs around non-rotating black holes – an analytical study
arxiv-2111-13592.creator: Arpan Krishna Mitra, Aishee Chakraborty, Pratik Tarafdar, Tapas Kumar Das
arxiv-2111-13592.description: Abstract Low angular momentum, general relativistic, axially symmetric accretion of hydrodynamic fluid onto Schwarzschild black holes may undergo more than one critical transition. To obtain the stationary integral solutions corresponding to such multi-critical accretion flow, one needs to employ numerical solutions of the corresponding fluid dynamics equations.

arxiv-2211-16303.title: Darcy’s Law for Porous Media with Multiple Microstructures
arxiv-2211-16303.creator: Zhongwei Shen
arxiv-2211-16303.description: Abstract In this paper we study the homogenization of the Dirichlet problem for the Stokes equations in a perforated domain with multiple microstructures. First, under the assumption that the interface between subdomains is a union of Lipschitz surfaces, we show that the effective velocity and pressure are governed by a Darcy law, where the permeability matrix is piecewise constant.

arxiv-2308-00493.title: Uniform attachment with freezing
arxiv-2308-00493.creator: Étienne Bellin, Arthur Blanc-Renaudie, Emmanuel Kammerer, Igor Kortchemski
arxiv-2308-00493.description: Abstract In the classical model of random recursive trees, trees are recursively built by attaching new vertices to old ones. What happens if vertices are allowed to freeze, in the sense that new vertices cannot be attached to already frozen ones? We are interested in the impact of freezing on the height of such trees.

arxiv-2310-18491.title: Publicly-Detectable Watermarking for Language Models
arxiv-2310-18491.creator: Jaiden Fairoze, Sanjam Garg, Somesh Jha, Saeed Mahloujifar, Mohammad Mahmoody, Mingyuan Wang
arxiv-2310-18491.description: Abstract We present a publicly-detectable watermarking scheme for LMs: the detection algorithm contains no secret information, and it is executable by anyone. We embed a publicly-verifiable cryptographic signature into LM output using rejection sampling and prove that this produces unforgeable and distortion-free (i.e., undetectable without access to the public key) text output.

arxiv-2404-03950.title: Matchings in the hypercube with specified edges
arxiv-2404-03950.creator: Joshua Erde
arxiv-2404-03950.description: Abstract Given a matching M M in the hypercube Q n Q^{n} , the profile of M M is the vector 𝒙 = ( x 1 , … , x n ) ∈ ℕ n \bm{x}=(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n})\in\mathbb{N}^{n} such that M M contains x i x_{i} edges whose endpoints differ in the i i th coordinate.

arxiv-2506-04237.title: A Comprehensive Survey on the Risks and Limitations of Concept-based Models
arxiv-2506-04237.creator: Sanchit Sinha, Aidong Zhang
arxiv-2506-04237.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sanchit Sinha, Aidong Zhang. Concept-based Models are a class of inherently explainable networks that improve upon standard Deep Neural Networks by providing a rationale behind their predictions using human-understandable ‘concepts’. With these models being highly successful in critical applications like medical diagnosis and financial risk prediction, there is a natural push toward their wider adoption in sensitive domains to instill greater trust among diverse stakeholders.

pmc-11478650.title: Shrimp Larvae Counting Based on Improved YOLOv5 Model with Regional Segmentation
pmc-11478650.creator: Hongchao Duan, Jun Wang, Yuan Zhang, Xiangyu Wu, Tao Peng, Xuhao Liu, Delong Deng
pmc-11478650.description: Counting shrimp larvae is an essential part of shrimp farming. Due to their tiny size and high density, this task is exceedingly difficult. Thus, we introduce an algorithm for counting densely packed shrimp larvae utilizing an enhanced You Only Look Once version 5 (YOLOv5) model through a regional segmentation approach.

pmc-13315674.title: The carbohydrate-binding module of TrCel7A aids in navigating hemicellulose barriers in plant cell walls
pmc-13315674.creator: Nerya Zexer, Alec Paradiso, Anuleka Dutta, Daguan Nong, Gabriel Valentin, Parveen Kumar Deralia, Paul Dupree, William O. Hancock, Charles T. Anderson
pmc-13315674.description: Efficient enzymatic deconstruction of plant cell walls is critical for the utilization of lignocellulose biomass. Key enzymes in this process are cellobiohydrolases, a class of cellulases that processively degrade crystalline cellulose. Many cellobiohydrolases possess a carbohydrate-binding module (CBM), yet the specific roles of CBMs in substrate interaction remains unclear.

pmc-13431286.title: DeSpaST: deconvoluting spatial transcriptomics signals to cell-level resolution using histology images
pmc-13431286.creator: Qin Zhou, Shidan Wang, Yi Jiang, Yang Liu, Tingyi Wanyan, Kenian Chen, Zhuoyu Wen, Zhikai Chi, Peiran Quan, Kevin Lutz, Ruichen Rong, Lin Xu, Guanghua Xiao, Yang Xie
pmc-13431286.description: Advances in spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies enable spatially resolved gene expression profiling, yet most platforms remain limited to spot-level resolution, where each measurement aggregates signals from multiple cells and obscures cell-specific programs and microenvironmental interactions. Existing computational approaches either provide limited sub-spot refinement or rely on matched single-cell RNA sequencing references that are costly and difficult to obtain.
